title: Cost Accounting Systems
outcomes: Record transactions in non-integrated cost ledgers.
Explain integrated accounting and its pre-requisites.
Reconcile costing profit with financial profit.

meta.exam_tip: In reconciliation, write a one-word reason ("financial only", "over-absorbed") next to each item to fix its direction.

concepts.title: Non-integrated (cost ledger) accounting
body: In non-integrated (cost ledger) accounting, cost records are kept separately from financial books. Only cost items (materials, labour, overheads, sales) enter the cost ledger; purely financial items such as interest received, dividends, profits or losses on fixed assets and income-tax are left out.

Main accounts: Cost Ledger Control Account (also called General Ledger Adjustment Account) — the link with financial books, recording items whose double entry is in the financial ledger; Stores Ledger Control; Wages Control; Production, Administration and Selling Overhead Control; Work-in-Progress Control; Finished Goods Control; Cost of Sales; and Costing Profit and Loss Account.

Typical entries: purchases — Dr Stores Ledger Control, Cr Cost Ledger Control; materials issued — Dr WIP Control, Cr Stores Ledger Control; wages paid — Dr Wages Control, Cr Cost Ledger Control; overheads absorbed — Dr WIP, Cr Overhead Control; completed output — Dr Finished Goods, Cr WIP; sales — Dr Cost Ledger Control, Cr Costing P&L.
Under- or over-absorbed overheads are transferred to the Costing Profit and Loss Account (or carried forward if seasonal).
concepts.analogy: The cost ledger is a self-balancing mirror of the factory, linked to the main books through one control account.
concepts.work: When wages of ₹50,000 are paid, the cost ledger shows Wages Control Dr and Cost Ledger Control Cr — the bank side lives in the financial books.

concepts.title: Integrated accounting
body: Integrated accounting keeps one set of books that provides both financial and cost information; there is no need to reconcile two profits.

Accounts like bank, debtors, creditors and fixed assets sit alongside stores control, WIP control and overhead control accounts; entries for cash and credit transactions go straight to the real accounts instead of a cost ledger control account.

Pre-requisites: management decision on the extent of integration, suitable coding, agreed treatment of items such as stock valuation and overheads, and a well-designed system for periodic reports. Advantages: no duplication, lower cost, no reconciliation and quicker information.
concepts.analogy: One ledger, two uses: it closes the financial year and also tells managers what each product costs.
concepts.work: Purchasing raw material on credit in integrated books: Dr Stores Ledger Control, Cr Creditors.

concepts.title: Reconciling cost and financial profit
body: When cost and financial books are separate, the two profits differ and are reconciled in a memorandum statement.

Reasons: items only in financial books (interest, dividends, rent received, profit or loss on sale of assets, fines, income-tax, write-offs of goodwill or preliminary expenses); items only in cost books (notional rent or interest charged in costing); under- or over-absorption of overheads; and different stock valuation methods.

Method: start with one profit, add items that increase the other profit, deduct items that decrease it. Over-absorption means cost profit is lower, so it is added when moving to financial profit; under-absorption the reverse.
concepts.analogy: Reconciliation explains every rupee of difference so both sets of books can be trusted.
concepts.work: Notional rent of ₹30,000 charged in costing makes cost profit lower; add it back to reach financial profit.

illustrations.title: Why do the two profits differ?
illustrations.q: Costing profit of Rana Ltd. is ₹4,12,000. Differences: (i) factory overheads under-absorbed in cost accounts ₹25,000; (ii) office overheads over-absorbed ₹12,000; (iii) dividend received ₹18,000 (financial books only); (iv) closing stock valued ₹9,000 higher in financial books than in cost books (opening stocks equal); (v) loss on sale of a machine ₹6,000 (financial books only). Prepare a reconciliation and find the financial profit.

solution.title: Reconciliation statement

solution.text: Rule of thumb: start from costing profit; add items that make financial profit higher, deduct those that make it lower.

illustrations.title: Work-in-progress control account
illustrations.q: Under non-integrated accounts: opening WIP ₹60,000; materials issued to production ₹2,40,000; direct wages charged ₹1,80,000; production overheads absorbed ₹1,50,000; cost of finished goods transferred ₹5,20,000. Prepare the WIP control account and find the closing balance.

jobs.title: Month-end reconciliation
jobs.situation: The plant controller asks why cost profit exceeds book profit by ₹2 lakh.
steps: List items only in financial books.
Compare overhead absorbed with actual overhead.
Compare stock values in both sets.
Prepare the reconciliation and investigate unexplained differences.
jobs.takeaway: Over- and under-absorption and stock valuation explain most differences.

mcqs.q: In non-integrated accounts, the account that links cost and financial books is:
mcqs.explain: The Cost Ledger Control (General Ledger Adjustment) Account records items whose other side lies in the financial books. In practice: it keeps the cost ledger self-balancing.

mcqs.q: Materials issued to production are recorded as:
options: Dr WIP Control, Cr Stores Ledger Control
Dr Stores Ledger Control, Cr WIP Control
Dr Cost Ledger Control, Cr Stores
mcqs.explain: Issues move cost from stores into production. In practice: indirect materials go to overhead control instead.

mcqs.q: Which item appears only in financial books?
mcqs.explain: Dividends are financial income with no link to production cost. In practice: add it to costing profit to reach financial profit.

mcqs.q: Factory overheads over-absorbed in cost accounts mean financial profit is:
mcqs.explain: Over-absorption charges more cost in cost books than was actually incurred, so cost profit is lower. In practice: add it when going to financial profit.

mcqs.q: In integrated accounts, a credit purchase of materials is recorded as:
options: Dr Stores Ledger Control, Cr Creditors
Dr Stores Ledger Control, Cr Cost Ledger Control
mcqs.explain: Integrated books post directly to personal and real accounts; there is no cost ledger control account. In practice: one trial balance serves both needs.

mcqs.q: Notional rent charged in cost accounts:
options: Makes cost profit lower than financial profit
mcqs.explain: Notional charges exist only in costing, reducing cost profit. In practice: add back to reach financial profit.

mcqs.q: A key advantage of integrated accounts is:
options: No need to reconcile cost and financial profit
mcqs.explain: With one set of books, there is a single profit figure. In practice: requires agreed policies on stock and overheads.

mcqs.q: Under-absorbed production overhead at year end is usually transferred to:
mcqs.explain: Abnormal or year-end under-absorption is written off to Costing P&L (or adjusted via supplementary rates). In practice: seasonal amounts may be carried forward.

summary: Non-integrated: separate cost ledger linked by Cost Ledger Control A/c.
Integrated: one set of books, no reconciliation.
Differences: financial-only items, notional costs, over/under-absorption, stock valuation.
remember: Over-absorption → add to cost profit to reach financial profit.
traps: Dividends and asset gains never enter cost books.

viva.q: What is a cost ledger control account?
viva.model: An account in the cost ledger that records the other side of entries whose double entry is in the financial books, making the cost ledger self-balancing.

viva.q: Name items excluded from cost accounts.
viva.model: Purely financial items such as interest received, dividends, profit or loss on sale of fixed assets, fines and income-tax.
A system with one set of books giving both financial and cost information, so no reconciliation is needed.

viva.q: How does stock valuation cause a difference?
viva.model: If closing stock is valued higher in financial books than in cost books, financial profit is higher by that amount; opening stock works the opposite way.
They are transferred to the Costing Profit and Loss Account or recovered through supplementary rates.

cases.title: Sharma Castings
cases.case: Sharma Castings keeps separate cost books. For the year: costing profit ₹6,50,000; administration overheads under-absorbed ₹20,000; interest on bank deposits ₹15,000 (financial only); goodwill written off ₹40,000; notional interest on capital charged in costing ₹30,000.

mcqs.q: Effect of under-absorbed administration overheads on financial profit vs. cost profit:
mcqs.explain: Actual cost was higher than absorbed, so financial profit is lower. In practice: deduct it.

mcqs.q: Notional interest charged in costing is:
options: Added to cost profit to reach financial profit
mcqs.explain: It reduced cost profit but never appears in financial books. In practice: add back.

options: Remove the need for this reconciliation
mcqs.explain: One set of books produces one profit. In practice: overheads are still absorbed.
